note: Before: the original spec with one Cortex Analyst tool. Called through the SQL API it failed every question (391920, no execution environment), so it was run as a temporary copy with a warehouse. After runs were taken once the ontology search index had caught up with the Enterprise terms (about 6 hours after approval).

rows.question: What is a Legal Entity in our enterprise model?
rows.before: In our enterprise model, a Legal Entity is a golden company record: one operating company, identified by an SAP company code. It's the shared anchor that all the business apps tie their numbers to, so Finance, Sales, People, Spend, Working Capital and Supply Chain all report against the same company.
rows.after: In our enterprise model, a Legal Entity is a company code. It's the single master ("golden") record for the business unit that books revenue, owes suppliers and employs people.
rows.verdict: Governed definition of Enterprise.Legal Entity and its IS_A link to Org Unit, instead of a description assembled from the semantic view.

rows.question: Is a Supplier in the Enterprise model the same concept as in Supply Chain?
rows.before: Not quite. The Enterprise model's Supplier is a broader "golden" supplier.
rows.after: Yes, it's the same concept. The Enterprise model has no Supplier node of its own.
rows.verdict: Correct: Enterprise reuses Supply Chain.Supplier and adds Local Supplier (same as one golden Supplier). Before, it said they were different concepts.

rows.question: What kinds of party does the enterprise model have?
rows.before: The enterprise model has three kinds of party. Each one is a golden record that pulls together the local records for that party from the different apps: Customer (20 golden records, from 108 local records): matched across Finance (FIN), Sales (SAL), Supply Chain (SCM) and Working Capital (WCP).
rows.after: The enterprise model has three kinds of Party. Each one is an entity that is defined as "a kind of Party".
rows.verdict: Reads the governed IS_A Party links, with Party itself defined in the Supply Chain domain, instead of listing data tables.

rows.question: Which company has the best revenue per employee?
rows.before: Japan Operations has the highest revenue per employee, at about $36.9K. It has the smallest workforce of the three companies (403 people), and its revenue of $14.9M is close to the others'.
rows.after: Japan Operations (APAC) has the highest revenue per employee, about $36.9K: $14.89M of revenue across 403 employees. US Operations comes second at about $33.7K and EU Operations third at about $32.6K.
rows.verdict: Same figures (Japan Operations, about $36.9K per employee), now labelled Derived because no governed metric exists.

rows.question: Which suppliers have the most spend? Say which governed concept the number represents.
rows.before: Teledyne DALSA has the most spend at $321.6K. Coherent Corp is second ($279.2K), followed by Fabrikam Packaging ($264.5K), TRUMPF Lasertechnik ($262.9K) and Festo AG ($257.1K).
rows.after: Teledyne DALSA has the most spend, at about $322K. Coherent Corp is next at $279K, then Fabrikam Packaging at $264K.
rows.verdict: Same ranking, and it says plainly that supplier spend is not yet a governed concept: a gap to fill.

rows.question: How is an AP Invoice related to other entities?
rows.before: The Enterprise 360 model has no AP Invoice entity, so you can't trace individual invoices or their line-level links. Accounts payable appears only as totals: per supplier, and as a payment-days figure per legal entity.
rows.after: In the governed ontology, an AP Invoice is connected to two other entities: it is payable to a Supplier, and it is a kind of Transaction. Both links are active and governed, and the list of relationships is complete.
rows.verdict: Governed links from the ontology: AP Invoice is a kind of Transaction and is payable to a Supplier. Before, it said the model had no AP Invoice.

rows.question: What is Widget Velocity Quotient?
rows.before: I couldn't find "Widget Velocity Quotient" in the Enterprise 360 model. No metric, column or calculation by that name exists in Finance, Sales, People, Spend, Working Capital or Supply Chain 360, so I can't define it or calculate it from this data.
rows.after: I couldn't find a governed definition for "Widget Velocity Quotient" in the Business Ontology I can access. I searched for the full name and for the shorter "widget velocity", and neither returned anything.
rows.verdict: Searches the ontology first, then declines without substituting an industry definition.
